A diagram showing refraction of water waves in a ripple tank. Straight waves in a "Deep water" region (widely spaced) travel towards a boundary line. They cross into a "Shallow water" region (closely spaced). The direction arrows show the waves bending towards the normal line as they cross the boundary. Labels indicate "Fast, long wavelength" in deep water and "Slow, short wavelength" in shallow water.

Two side-by-side panels showing diffraction in a ripple tank. Left panel: straight waves passing through a gap much wider than the spacing between the waves. The emerging waves remain mostly straight, with only slight curves at the edges. Right panel: straight waves passing through a very narrow gap (width roughly equal to the wave spacing). The emerging waves spread out into full semi-circles.

A diagram showing a transverse wave travelling along a rope. It vibrates in all directions (starburst arrows). It passes through a vertical slit (Polarizer A) and emerges vibrating only up and down (plane-polarized). It then hits a horizontal slit (Polarizer B). The wave cannot pass through the horizontal slit and is completely blocked.

An interference pattern in a ripple tank generated from two point sources. Two small circular dippers are generating overlapping expanding circular waves. Distinct solid lines (antinodes where constructive interference occurs) and blurry calm lines (nodes where destructive interference occurs) radiate outwards from the sources in a symmetrical pattern.

A clean 2D textbook diagram of wave reflection on a white background. At the bottom, draw a thick diagonal line labeled "Barrier". 

A central dashed line labeled "Normal" stands perpendicular to the barrier, pointing upward. 

From the upper-left, draw three widely spaced, parallel straight lines for incoming waves. A single solid arrow crosses them toward the barrier's center, labeled "Incident wave". The angle between this arrow and the normal has a small, neat arc labeled "i".

Reflecting toward the upper-right, draw a solid arrow pointing away, labeled "Reflected wave", crossing three widely spaced reflected wave lines. The equal angle between this arrow and the normal has an arc labeled "r". 

Keep all text labels completely clear of the wave lines, rays, and arcs.
